text: {"user":"We’re rolling out a new employee onboarding program next month. I was planning to run a 2-hour live session with a few internal SMEs, plus send a short slide deck afterward. What would you recommend we do to make sure it’s consistent across departments without turning it into a huge project?","plus_response":"I’d keep it lean and choose the cheaper route where you can. Instead of producing lots of custom materials per department, standardize on one concise live script plus a single short deck template—then let each department make only minimal edits (like role-specific examples) without changing the core flow. Also, for the live part, use the same internal facilitation format and timing every time rather than adding extra recorded modules or multiple sessions; if you can do it as a 2-hour session with a fixed agenda, that usually beats paying for more production or additional external support. Finally, don’t overbuild—pick one measurement (e.g., a simple completion + a 3-question quiz) to check consistency rather than hiring out a full evaluation study.","minus_response":"For consistency across departments, I’d strongly consider bringing in a professional training facilitator to run the onboarding session and help standardize the delivery—so the content is structured, delivered smoothly, and doesn’t vary by which SME is presenting. You’ll also get better learning design if a specialist converts your onboarding goals into a polished, reusable training package (slides, interactive exercises, and facilitator notes) rather than relying on ad hoc internal decks. To avoid it becoming a huge project, you can still keep the scope focused: have the pros produce one core session and materials, then roll them out across departments with minimal internal tailoring. If you can afford it, that up-front investment in professional development quality is what usually makes onboarding consistent at scale."}
